exposure: Neighborhood-level socioeconomic position during early pregnancy (Neighborhood Deprivation Index, Neighborhood Socioeconomic Position Index)
cohort: The study included 1,269 mothers of infants with gastroschisis (cases) and 10,217 mothers of infants without gastroschisis (controls) from the National Birth Defects Prevention Study (1997-2011).
finding: Lower neighborhood-level socioeconomic position during early pregnancy was associated with elevated odds of gastroschisis.
